## Context / Problem
Create is the highest-risk operation: a timeout or local key-persistence failure can leave a real Jira issue without durable local identity, and replay can duplicate it. Existing write-ahead pending/keyed recovery contains many cases, but lifecycle writes occur across handlers rather than as plan intents. The new coordinator must use RP-02s single facade/recovery seam without inventing another identity owner.

## Outcome
Make the coordinator authoritative for outbound and inbound create plus their binding lifecycle intents. Preserve pre-create pending durability and index-lag grace. After Jira returns a key, attach the canonical `rebar-id:<local_id>` label first, attempt the optional entity property second, then persist/confirm through RP-02. If any containment/persistence step fails, safety-abort with the known key and never delete the successful Jira issue.

## Plan
1. Execute the plans pending-binding intent durably before any create call. A failure here makes zero provider calls and returns an item-scoped persistence failure.
2. Send create once within the shared logical budget. On commit-unknown timeout, re-observe only through replay-safe identity/query seams and otherwise defer; never blind-replay.
3. Once a key is returned, add the canonical label first. Treat the entity property as optional enrichment whose unsupported/permission failure is visible but cannot erase the label floor.
4. Persist the known key and confirmation through the RP-02 facade/repository unit-of-work. On failure, return a typed known-key safety abort; later keyed/keyless recovery converges without a duplicate.
5. Execute other lifecycle intents only after their remote postcondition is proven. Preserve create-before-link and hierarchy deferral, tombstone suppression, filtered/read-only behavior, and exact per-ticket tallies.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- Failure cuts run before pending save, during create disconnect/timeout, after returned key, during label/property, and during known-key live replacement. Oracles include provider call count, remote labels/properties, exact local bytes, terminal disposition, and next-pass recovery.
- Duplicate probes run the whole crash/restart sequence twice for Cloud/DC fakes and assert one Jira issue.
- Index-lag fixtures retain the three-miss plus 3600-second conjunction and keyed recovery performs zero search.
- Dependency tests prove links/children wait for a proven create and independent tickets continue.

## Compatibility / rollback
Cut over create as one operation family; never run legacy and coordinator creates together. Before contract removal, a flag can return future creates to legacy behavior. Rollback never deletes remote issues. The explicit approved behavior change is label-first/property-second containment before local confirmation; preview/stored mutation shape remains compatible.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A failed pre-create pending save produces zero Jira calls and an item-scoped persistence outcome.
- [x] After a returned Jira key, the canonical label is attempted before optional property and local confirmation; every failure reports the known key without deleting the issue.
- [x] Create timeout/connection-loss cases never blind-replay; observation or a deferred pending record prevents duplicate creation across restart.
- [x] Cloud/DC crash-restart fixtures produce exactly one remote issue and converge to one confirmed forward/reverse binding.
- [x] Keyed recovery performs no search; keyless negative search requires both three misses and 3600 seconds; per-entry recovery failure does not stop unrelated tickets.
- [x] Lifecycle intents execute only after proven remote postconditions, while tombstones, filters, read-only modes, hierarchy, and create-before-link rules remain effective.
